examples.fr: Tu viens ce soir ? Chais pas, on verra.
examples.en: You coming tonight? Dunno, we'll see.

notes: Heavy contraction of je ne sais pas. Spoken only, never written outside dialogue.

examples.fr: Je ne sais pas où il habite.
examples.en: I don't know where he lives.

notes: The neutral form. Safe in writing and any formal speech.

examples.fr: La raison de son départ, je l'ignore.
examples.en: As to the reason for his departure, I cannot say.

notes: Sounds slightly cold or official. Common in journalism and administrative speech.

examples.fr: Je suis crevé, je vais me coucher.
examples.en: I'm knackered, I'm off to bed.

notes: Adjective agrees with the subject (crevée for feminine).

examples.fr: Tu as l'air fatigué, ça va ?
examples.en: You look tired, are you alright?

notes: Neutral, fits any context.

examples.fr: Éreinté par cette journée, il s'effondra dans le fauteuil.
examples.en: Worn out by the day, he collapsed into the armchair.

examples.fr: Les soldats rentraient éreintés du front.
examples.en: The soldiers returned from the front utterly spent.

examples.fr: Éreinté mais content, il acheva enfin son manuscrit.
examples.en: Exhausted but pleased, he at last completed his manuscript.

notes: Literally suggests a broken back. Visual and a little dramatic.

examples.fr: J'ai plus de thune jusqu'à la fin du mois.
examples.en: I'm skint until the end of the month.

examples.fr: Prête-moi un peu de thune, je te rends ça demain.
examples.en: Lend us a bit of cash, I'll pay you back tomorrow.

examples.fr: Faut de la thune pour vivre à Paris.
examples.en: You need dosh to live in Paris.

notes: Very common in spoken French, especially among under 40s.

examples.fr: Je n'ai pas assez d'argent pour ça.
examples.en: I don't have enough money for that.

notes: The neutral term.

examples.fr: Il comptait ses deniers avec soin.
examples.en: He counted his coins with care.

examples.fr: Le vieil avare gardait ses deniers sous le matelas.
examples.en: The old miser kept his pennies beneath the mattress.

examples.fr: Sans deniers ni soutien, elle dut quitter Paris.
examples.en: Without funds or support, she was obliged to leave Paris.

notes: Archaic. Found in 19th century novels or deliberately old fashioned writing.

examples.fr: Salut, ça va ?
examples.en: Hey, how are you?

notes: Only with people you tutoie. Works any time of day.

examples.fr: Bonsoir madame, une table pour deux.
examples.en: Good evening, a table for two.

notes: Standard evening greeting from roughly late afternoon onward.

examples.fr: Je vous salue, monsieur le directeur.
examples.en: Good day to you, Director.

notes: Quite formal, slightly archaic in everyday use. Survives in fixed phrases.

examples.fr: On y va ? Carrément !
examples.en: Shall we go? Absolutely!

notes: Strong agreement, very common in spoken French.

examples.fr: On se voit demain ? D'accord.
examples.en: See you tomorrow? Agreed.

notes: The workhorse. Safe everywhere.

examples.fr: Vous êtes bien monsieur Dupont ? Tout à fait.
examples.en: You are Monsieur Dupont? Indeed I am.

notes: Slightly formal, polite, very common in service contexts.

examples.fr: On mange quand ? J'ai la dalle !
examples.en: When are we eating? I'm starving!

examples.fr: T'as pas un truc à grignoter ? J'ai la dalle.
examples.en: Got anything to nibble on? I'm famished.

examples.fr: Après cette rando, j'avais une de ces dalles !
examples.en: After that hike, I had such an appetite!

notes: Very common slang. La dalle literally means a slab or paving stone.

examples.fr: J'ai faim, on va déjeuner ?
examples.en: I'm hungry, shall we have lunch?

notes: The standard form.

examples.fr: Je meurs de faim, vivement le dîner.
examples.en: I'm starving, roll on dinner.

notes: Hyperbolic but extremely common.

examples.fr: Ses excuses, ça me saoule.
examples.en: His excuses, I'm sick of them.

examples.fr: Ça me saoule de devoir tout recommencer.
examples.en: Having to start over is doing my head in.

examples.fr: Sa façon de parler, ça me saoule au plus haut point.
examples.en: The way he talks gets right on my nerves.

notes: From saouler, to get drunk. Now means to irritate intensely. Very common.

examples.fr: Ça m'énerve quand il est en retard.
examples.en: It annoys me when he's late.

notes: The everyday term.

examples.fr: Cette désinvolture m'agace au plus haut point.
examples.en: This casualness irritates me greatly.

notes: Cooler, more controlled register. Note cela instead of ça.

examples.fr: Je kiffe ce groupe.
examples.en: I'm really into this band.

examples.fr: Tu kifferais l'ambiance, c'est trop bien.
examples.en: You'd love the vibe, it's so good.

examples.fr: Il kiffe grave la cuisine japonaise.
examples.en: He's mad about Japanese food.

notes: From Arabic kif (pleasure). Strong slang, very common among younger speakers.

examples.fr: J'aime bien ce film.
examples.en: I quite like this film.

notes: The standard way to say like. Without bien, aimer leans toward love.

examples.fr: J'apprécie beaucoup votre travail.
examples.en: I greatly appreciate your work.

notes: Polite, measured. Common in professional contexts.

examples.fr: Il a fallu raquer 50 balles pour entrer.
examples.en: We had to fork out 50 quid to get in.

examples.fr: J'en peux plus de raquer pour cet abonnement.
examples.en: I'm done coughing up for this subscription.

examples.fr: C'est toi qui raques cette fois ?
examples.en: You picking up the tab this time?

notes: Slightly grudging tone. Implies the price was annoying.

examples.fr: Je vais payer l'addition.
examples.en: I'll pay the bill.

notes: The neutral term.

examples.fr: Il s'est acquitté de sa dette le mois dernier.
examples.en: He discharged his debt last month.

notes: Formal, often financial or legal. Implies fulfilling an obligation.

examples.fr: T'as pigé ce qu'il a dit ?
examples.en: Did you get what he said?

examples.fr: J'ai rien pigé à son explication.
examples.en: I didn't get a word of his explanation.

examples.fr: Elle pige vite, cette gamine.
examples.en: She catches on quickly, that kid.

notes: Very common spoken. Often used in the negative: j'ai rien pigé.

examples.fr: Je comprends ce que tu veux dire.
examples.en: I understand what you mean.

notes: Workhorse verb.

examples.fr: Je saisis mal la nuance que vous évoquez.
examples.en: I cannot quite grasp the nuance you are alluding to.

notes: Implies catching a subtle or intellectual point. Common in academic and formal contexts.

examples.fr: J'ai bossé jusqu'à minuit hier.
examples.en: I grafted till midnight yesterday.

examples.fr: Tu bosses où en ce moment ?
examples.en: Where are you working these days?

examples.fr: Faut bosser dur si on veut y arriver.
examples.en: We've got to graft hard if we want to make it.

notes: Extremely common spoken French for to work. Not vulgar, just informal.

examples.fr: Il travaille dur pour soutenir sa famille.
examples.en: He works hard to support his family.

notes: The standard neutral form.

examples.fr: Il s'évertue à résoudre ce problème depuis des semaines.
examples.en: He has been striving to resolve this problem for weeks.

notes: Implies persistent effort against difficulty. Common in writing.

examples.fr: On se fait suer ici, on s'en va ?
examples.en: We're bored stiff here, shall we head off?

notes: Literally to make oneself sweat. Conveys restless boredom.

examples.fr: Les enfants s'ennuient en attendant.
examples.en: The children are getting bored waiting.

notes: The neutral verb.

examples.fr: Il languissait dans sa province natale.
examples.en: He languished in his native province.

examples.fr: Loin d'elle, il languissait sans cesse.
examples.en: Far from her, he pined without ceasing.

examples.fr: Que de jours à languir dans cette pension morne !
examples.en: How many days spent languishing in that dreary boarding house!

notes: Suggests soulful weariness or pining. Beautiful in literary contexts, overwrought in casual ones.
